title: Sinking the evil in the river

dating.label: Achaemenid · Neo-Assyrian witnesses
dating.note: The linked source witnesses carry Achaemenid, Neo-Assyrian period labels. These date surviving manuscripts, not the composition.

purpose: At the riverbank the paralysed, bewitched man appeals to the divine judge, dips three times in the river in a textile, asks the river to carry the evil down to the underworld waters, is bathed, and touches a brewer's vat and his gate on the way home.
attribution: Apotropaic ritual (namburbi) instruction; the practitioner and the sick man act

phases.name: At the riverbank
phases.idea: The ground is prepared, a libation poured, figures made and the sick man stands before the god.

phases.name: Appeal
phases.idea: The incantation asks that the evil be carried off.

phases.name: In the river
phases.idea: Beer is poured to the river, the man dips three times, asks the river to take the evil, and is bathed.

phases.name: Return home
phases.idea: He touches a brewer's vat and his own gate.

steps.title: Sweep and sprinkle the riverbank
steps.shortDescription: On a favourable day, at the riverbank, the ground is beaten (swept) and sprinkled with pure water.
steps.summary: On a favourable day, at the riverbank, the ground is beaten (swept) and sprinkled with pure water.
steps.evidence: Line 5 glosses "on a favourable day, at the bank of the river, ground beat, pure water sprinkle". "Beat the ground" is taken as sweeping; that reading is conventional but not stated by the gloss.

image.alt: Illustrative reconstruction: sweep and sprinkle the riverbank.
image.note: Illustrative reconstruction of the documented objects and action; form, colour and staging beyond the glossed text are conjectural.

steps.title: Set up an altar and pour a libation
steps.shortTitle: Set up an altar and pour a libation
steps.shortDescription: A portable altar is set up before the god and a libation is poured.
steps.summary: A portable altar is set up before the god and a libation is poured.
steps.evidence: End of line 5 and start of line 6 gloss "before (god) portable altar … libation pour; (libation vessel) …". The god is written with a sign rendered "1" in the glosses; the incantation (line 8) calls him judge of heaven and earth. The phrase about a binding in line 6 is unclear and not mapped.

steps.title: Sink three times in the river in a textile
steps.shortTitle: Sink three times in the river in a textile
steps.shortDescription: The sick man, with a textile, sinks into the river three times.
steps.summary: The sick man, with a textile, sinks into the river three times.
steps.evidence: Line 19 glosses "sick … textile thrice in river sink". Whether the textile is worn or held is not clear from the glosses; line 20 adds "upstream slip into river", and line 26 has him come up and the textile torn off, so the textile functions as a carrier left behind.

steps.title: Ask the river to carry the evil away
steps.shortTitle: Ask the river to carry the evil away
steps.shortDescription: In the incantation to the river he asks it to take away the evil and carry it down to the underground waters, so that it not come near him or his house.
steps.summary: In the incantation to the river he asks it to take away the evil and carry it down to the underground waters, so that it not come near him or his house.
steps.evidence: Line 24 glosses "evil take away, river, go down (cosmic) underground water; evil … to me and house not come close". Classed as petition (to the river) and binding (evil not to approach).

steps.title: Come up, tear off the textile, bathe
steps.shortTitle: Come up, tear off the textile, bathe
steps.shortDescription: After three recitations he comes up, the textile is torn away, and he is bathed from a holy-water vessel while an incantation is recited; then another textile.
steps.summary: After three recitations he comes up, the textile is torn away, and he is bathed from a holy-water vessel while an incantation is recited; then another textile.
steps.evidence: Line 26 glosses "thrice say, go up, textile tear away, holy water vessel over him bathe, incantation 'strip off' count, textile (an)other". The last words probably mean he puts on another textile; not mapped.

steps.title: Touch the gate with gypsum and bitumen
steps.shortTitle: Touch the gate with gypsum and bitumen
steps.shortDescription: The gate is touched with gypsum and bitumen; this concludes the apotropaic ritual.
steps.summary: The gate is touched with gypsum and bitumen; this concludes the apotropaic ritual.
steps.evidence: Line 29 glosses "gypsum and bitumen gate touch, apotropaic ritual". Whose gate is inferred from lines 27–28 (his house). Existing action type anoint-door is reused though the material is gypsum and bitumen, not oil.
